newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: IMF says no immediate cash for Zimbabwe reforms.
newsitem.headline: IMF says no immediate cash for Zimbabwe reforms.

text.p: Zimbabwe will not get any immediate funding from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for a five-year economic reform programme it plans to launch later this year, a senior IMF official said on Monday.

Michael Nowak, division chief for the IMF Southern African Department, said President Robert Mugabe's government might, however, get some crucial aid in the financial year starting next July after moving on, and providing detailed plans on how it intended to fight runaway state spending and a big budget deficit.
"The IMF is ready to assist once this area has been addressed," Nowak told a news conference in Harare.

"The process is long...and I think we should be looking at mid-1997, in the new financial year," he said to queries on how soon Harare -- which government officials and econonomic analysts say is desperate for IMF and World Bank aid -- could get assistance for its new five-year Zimbabwe Programme for Economic and Social Transformation (ZIMPREST).
